lesson.content:
## What it is
IPv4 addressing is a system where each host on a network is assigned a 32-bit address, typically written in dotted decimal format, such as 192.168.1.10. This system divides the address space into classes A, B, and C, which are further subdivided using subnetting to create smaller, more manageable subnets. [p. 2]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine you have a water tank that fills up at a constant rate and leaks out at a constant rate. If the tank is full, any additional water spills out. In networking, each host has a queue that fills up with packets at a constant rate, and any packets arriving when the queue is full are discarded. This ensures that the queue doesn't overflow, maintaining a smooth, fixed-rate flow of packets. [p. 2]

## How it works
1. **IP Address Assignment**: Each host is assigned a 32-bit IP address, which is a logical address used by the network layer to identify hosts on a network. [p. 2]
2. **Subnetting**: Bits from the host part of the IP address are borrowed to create smaller subnets. The subnet mask (e.g., 255.255.255.0 or /24) indicates which bits are the network part. [p. 2]
3. **Addressing Classes**: The IP address space is divided into classes A, B, and C, with classful addressing. Classes A, B, and C are used for unicast addressing, while class E is reserved. [p. 2]

## Key terms
- **IP Address**: A 32-bit address given by the network to reach hosts on any network. [p. 2]
- **Subnet Mask**: A 32-bit mask used to determine which part of the IP address represents the network part. [p. 2]

## Example
Consider an IP address 192.168.1.10 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0. The subnet mask indicates that the first three parts (192.168.1) represent the network part, and the fourth part (10) represents the host part. This allows for 254 usable host addresses in the subnet (2^8 - 2). [p. 2]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 2]

## Exam tip
Be able to explain the difference between IP addresses and MAC addresses, and how subnetting works to create smaller subnets. Understand the concept of bursty traffic and how the token bucket algorithm manages it. [p. 2]
